plan: Ten new items, topics searched first (WIC keys checked against the bank's existing WIC answers): tenuous/incremental WIC, monarch relay central idea, sloth-moth inference, wheat two-part data, jazz cross-text, appositive comma, semicolon, 'Similarly,', fire-adapted trees generalization synthesis.

passages.title: One shared style
passages.text: The proposed link between the two ancient settlements remains ______: it rests entirely on a single shared pottery style, which could just as easily have spread between unrelated communities through trade.

passages.title: Slow gains
passages.text: Rather than arriving in a sudden breakthrough, the improvement in phone battery life over the past decade has been ______, with each new generation lasting only slightly longer than the one before it.

passages.title: A relay across generations
passages.text: Each fall, monarch butterflies from eastern North America fly as far as 4,000 kilometers to forests in central Mexico, where they spend the winter. In spring they head north, but no individual completes the return. The butterflies breed along the way, and it is their children and grandchildren that continue the journey and reach the northern United States and Canada. The monarchs that fly south again in the fall may therefore be the great-grandchildren of those that left Mexico in spring.

passages.title: A risky descent
passages.text: Three-toed sloths spend nearly all their lives in trees, yet about once a week they climb down to the ground to defecate, a trip that exposes them to predators. Researchers have found that moths living in sloth fur lay their eggs in the dung. The moths later return to the fur, where they appear to add nutrients that help algae grow there, and sloths sometimes eat that algae. Based on these findings, the researchers proposed that the risky descent ______

passages.title: Three wheat varieties
passages.text:
Researchers grew three varieties of wheat on 10 farms and recorded each variety's yield, in metric tons per hectare.
Variety | Average yield | Lowest yield | Highest yield
A | 4.1 | 3.8 | 4.4
B | 4.3 | 3.6 | 4.9
C | 4.6 | 2.9 | 6.0
The researchers claim that variety C produced the highest yields on average but was also the least consistent from farm to farm.

passages.title: Composed on the spot? (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A music critic describes jazz improvisation as composition in its purest form: a soloist invents an entirely new melody in the moment, with nothing prepared in advance.

Text 2
Studies of recorded jazz solos have found that experienced players frequently reuse short melodic phrases, often called licks, that they practiced beforehand. Skilled improvisers combine and vary these familiar phrases in new ways as they respond to the music around them.

passages.title: A first program
passages.text: Ada Lovelace, a mathematician by ______ wrote in 1843 a set of notes on a proposed calculating machine that included what many historians consider the first published computer program.

passages.title: Sold out
passages.text: By noon the bakery had sold every loaf of bread ______ by evening, even the last tray of pastries was gone.

passages.title: Reading in two directions
passages.text: Readers of English scan each line from left to right, and studies of eye movements show that they tend to look slightly ahead, to the right, of the word they are reading. ______ readers of Hebrew and Arabic, which are written from right to left, tend to look slightly ahead to the left.

passages.title: Trees and fire
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The cones of lodgepole pines are often sealed with resin that melts in the heat of a fire, releasing seeds onto the burned ground.
• Jack pines also have cones that open mainly after exposure to fire.
• Some eucalyptus trees sprout new shoots from buds under their bark after a fire.
• All three kinds of trees grow in places where wildfires occur regularly.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: it rests entirely on a single shared pottery style
candidates.explanation: A connection supported by one piece of evidence that could be explained another way is weak: "tenuous."

A.rationale: A link resting on one piece of evidence that has another explanation is far from indisputable.

C.rationale: "Obsolete" means outdated; nothing suggests the idea has been replaced.

D.rationale: "Deliberate" means intentional, which does not describe how strong a link is.

hints: Is the link strongly or weakly supported?
candidates.remember: The explanation after the colon tells you the strength of the claim.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: with each new generation lasting only slightly longer than the one before it
candidates.explanation: Small, steady gains from one generation to the next are "incremental."

A.rationale: "Abrupt" means sudden, the opposite of the gradual change described.

B.rationale: "Erratic" means irregular; the text describes steady small gains.

C.rationale: "Unprecedented" means never seen before, which the modest gains do not suggest.

hints: How big is each step of improvement?
candidates.remember: Contrast words like "rather than" point to the opposite of what follows them.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: protects the sloths from the predators that hunt them in the treetops.
choices.B: is mainly a way for sloths to find mates on the forest floor.
choices.C: may sustain a moth-and-algae partnership that adds to the sloths' diet.
choices.D: allows sloths to remove the moths that damage their fur.

candidates.evidence: where they appear to add nutrients that help algae grow there, and sloths sometimes eat that algae
candidates.explanation: The descent lets moths lay eggs in the dung; the moths then help algae grow in the fur, and sloths eat the algae, so the risky trip may be part of a beneficial cycle.

A.rationale: The text says the trip exposes sloths to predators.

B.rationale: Nothing in the text concerns mating.

D.rationale: The text suggests the moths may benefit sloths, not damage them.

hints: What do the moths, the algae and the sloths each get from the cycle?

strategy.explanation: Rule out choices that contradict the text.

candidates.remember: Follow a chain of causes to its end.

candidates.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researchers' claim?

choices.A: Variety C had the highest single yield of any variety, 6.0 metric tons per hectare.
choices.B: Variety A had the smallest difference between its lowest and highest yields.
choices.C: Variety B had a higher average yield than variety A did, 4.3 compared with 4.1.
choices.D: C averaged 4.6 tons, the most, and its yields spanned 3.1 tons, the widest range.

candidates.evidence: variety C produced the highest yields on average but was also the least consistent
candidates.explanation: The claim has two parts. D shows that C had the highest average (4.6) and the widest range (6.0 − 2.9 = 3.1 tons).

A.rationale: One high value supports neither the average nor the consistency part of the claim fully.

B.rationale: This concerns variety A's consistency, not variety C's average.

C.rationale: This compares A and B and says nothing about C.

hints: What two things does the claim say about variety C?
candidates.remember: Support both halves of a two-part claim.

candidates.stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the critic's description in Text 1?

choices.A: By arguing that improvisers often build solos from phrases they prepared in advance
choices.B: By agreeing that improvised solos contain nothing practiced beforehand
choices.C: By claiming that jazz soloists never respond to the other musicians
choices.D: By suggesting that recordings of jazz solos are rarely accurate

candidates.evidence: experienced players frequently reuse short melodic phrases, often called licks, that they practiced beforehand
candidates.explanation: Text 1 claims improvisation uses nothing prepared in advance; Text 2's research shows that soloists combine practiced phrases, which qualifies that claim.

B.rationale: Text 2 reports that players frequently reuse practiced phrases.

C.rationale: Text 2 says improvisers respond to the music around them.

D.rationale: Text 2 relies on recordings; it does not question them.

hints: What does Text 1 say about preparation, and what does Text 2 find?

strategy.explanation: Find the point where the texts disagree.

candidates.remember: Look for the specific claim in Text 1 that Text 2's evidence addresses.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.explanation: "A mathematician by training" is a nonessential appositive opened by a comma, so it must be closed by a comma before the verb "wrote."

A.rationale: Without a comma, the appositive "a mathematician by training" is not closed off from the verb "wrote."

B.rationale: A semicolon cannot separate a subject from its verb.

D.rationale: A dash cannot close an appositive that was opened with a comma.

hints: How does the phrase describing Lovelace begin?

strategy.explanation: Match the closing punctuation to the opening comma.

candidates.remember: An appositive opened with a comma closes with a comma.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: even the last tray of pastries was gone
candidates.explanation: "By noon the bakery had sold every loaf of bread" and "by evening, even the last tray of pastries was gone" are independent clauses, so a semicolon joins them.

A.rationale: A comma alone between two independent clauses is a comma splice.

C.rationale: "Which" cannot introduce the independent clause that follows.

D.rationale: A colon followed by "and" is not standard here.

hints: Can each side of the blank stand alone?

strategy.explanation: Check whether both sides are complete clauses.

candidates.remember: A semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses.

candidates.stem: The student wants to make a generalization about trees that grow where wildfires occur regularly. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Lodgepole pine cones are sealed with resin that melts in the heat of a fire.
choices.B: Jack pines have cones that open mainly after they are exposed to fire.
choices.C: After a fire, some eucalyptus trees sprout shoots from buds under their bark.
choices.D: Some trees in fire-prone places have traits that help them reproduce or regrow after a fire.

candidates.evidence: All three kinds of trees grow in places where wildfires occur regularly.
candidates.explanation: Only D draws a general statement from the three examples.

A.rationale: This describes one tree, not a generalization.

B.rationale: This describes one kind of tree.

C.rationale: This describes one group and makes no general statement.

hints: Which choice talks about trees in general rather than one kind?

strategy.explanation: The goal asks for a generalization.

candidates.remember: A generalization goes beyond any single example.

withdrawn.reason: withdrawn before review: a blind solver noted 'as far as 4,000 kilometers' understates the eastern monarch migration (up to about 4,500-4,800 km). Resubmit in the next SAT batch with the distance reworded.

item.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: No single monarch completes the yearly round trip; several generations do.
choices.B: Monarch butterflies spend the winter in forests in central Mexico.
choices.C: Monarchs fly farther each spring than they do each fall.
choices.D: Most monarch butterflies die before they reach central Mexico in the fall.

item.explanation: The text's focus is that the migration is a relay: the northbound trip is completed by later generations, and the fall migrants may be great-grandchildren of the spring migrants.

B.rationale: This is a detail from the first sentence, not the main idea.

C.rationale: The text does not compare the distances of the two journeys.

D.rationale: The text says nothing about how many monarchs fail to reach Mexico.

hints: What is surprising about who makes the return trip?

strategy.explanation: Summarize the text in one sentence.

item.remember: A main idea covers the whole text, not its opening detail.

withdrawn.reason: withdrawn before review: both blind solvers chose 'In contrast,' over the key 'Similarly,'; the left/right difference reads as a contrast, so the item is ambiguous. Not resubmitted.

item.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
item.evidence: they tend to look slightly ahead, to the right, of the word they are reading
item.explanation: In both cases, readers look slightly ahead in the direction they read; the second sentence describes a parallel pattern, so "Similarly" fits.

B.rationale: Looking ahead in the reading direction is the same habit in both cases, not a contrast.

C.rationale: English readers' habits do not cause Hebrew and Arabic readers' habits.

D.rationale: Hebrew and Arabic readers are not an example of English readers.

hints: Is the pattern for Hebrew and Arabic readers the same idea or the opposite idea?

strategy.explanation: Ask whether the underlying habit is the same.

item.remember: A surface difference (left vs. right) can hide a similarity in kind.
